s011-debug: A KeyError means the dict being accessed has no key 'email' at that point
Some records lack the 'email' key (missing/optional field, or key name differs by case/spelling/whitespace)
Diagnose by printing the offending record or its keys (and the traceback line) to see which record fails
Fix by using record.get('email') with a default, or checking 'email' in record before access
Handle or validate malformed/inconsistent input data (e.g., CSV header or JSON schema mismatch)
s012-debug: The error means something being called as a function at main.js:42 is actually undefined
Open DevTools and go to line 42 of main.js (click the link in console) to identify the call expression
Inspect each called identifier/method on that line (console.log or typeof) to find which is undefined
Common causes: typo in method name, wrong object/property, missing import or script not loaded, or script load order/timing
Use breakpoints/debugger and the call stack, or source maps if the code is minified, to trace where the value became undefined

docker ps로 같은 포트를 쓰는 실행 중인 컨테이너를 확인한다
lsof -i :포트 또는 netstat 등으로 호스트 프로세스가 점유 중인지 확인한다

브라우저는 다른 origin으로의 요청 시 응답에 Access-Control-Allow-Origin 헤더가 있어야 허용한다
서버(응답 측)에서 허용 origin 등 CORS 헤더를 설정하는 것이 근본적인 해결이다

s021-concept: A database index is a separate data structure (commonly a B-tree) that lets the database find rows without scanning the whole table
It stores column values with pointers to the corresponding rows, like a book's index
Speeds up reads/lookups, WHERE filters, joins and sorting on the indexed columns
Costs: extra storage and slower writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) since the index must be maintained
Should be chosen selectively for frequently queried columns; includes examples like primary key/unique indexes or composite indexes
s022-concept: Eventual consistency is a consistency model for distributed systems where replicas may temporarily differ
If no new updates are made, all replicas will eventually converge to the same value
Reads may return stale data in the interim
It trades strong consistency for higher availability and lower latency/partition tolerance (relates to CAP theorem)
Example: DNS, Dynamo-style/Cassandra stores, or social media counters; conflicts are resolved by e.g. last-write-wins or vector clocks
s023-concept: 클로저는 함수가 자신이 정의된 시점의 렌더링 범위(렉시컬 스코프)의 변수를 기억하고 접근하는 것이다
외부 함수가 종료된 후에도 내부 함수가 외부 변수에 접근할 수 있다
간단한 코드 예시(카운터 함수 등)로 설명된다
활용: 데이터 은닉/private 변수, 콜백, 함수 팩토리, 상태 유지
주의점: 루프에서의 변수 캡처 문제나 메모리 유지 가능성
s024-concept: OAuth는 권한 위임(authorization) 프레임워크로, 제3자 앱이 사용자의 비밀번호 없이 리소스에 접근하게 해준다
JWT는 클레임을 담아 서명한 토큰 포맷(형식)이다
둘은 같은 층위가 아니며, OAuth는 프로토콜/흐름이고 JWT는 토큰 표현 방식이다
OAuth의 액세스 토큰은 JWT로 구현할 수 있지만 반드시 그럴 필요는 없다(불투명 토큰도 가능)
JWT는 OAuth 없이도 자체 세션/인증 용도로 쓸 수 있으며, 인증(로그인)은 OpenID Connect가 담당한다
s025-concept: An operation is idempotent if making the same request multiple times has the same effect on server state as making it once
GET, PUT, DELETE (and HEAD/OPTIONS) are idempotent by HTTP spec; POST is not, and PATCH is not guaranteed
Idempotent does not mean identical response (e.g., DELETE may return 200 then 404)
Matters for safe retries after timeouts/network failures
POST can be made idempotent with an idempotency key; example like PUT setting a value vs POST creating a new resource each time
s031-decision: Recommend Postgres as the default for a small SaaS app
Reason: SaaS data is typically relational (users, orgs, subscriptions) and benefits from joins, transactions and constraints
Postgres also handles flexible/JSON data via JSONB, reducing the need for MongoDB
MongoDB fits when data is truly document-shaped, schema highly variable, or specific scale/ecosystem needs
Mention operational factors: managed hosting options, team familiarity, and ease of changing schema/migrations
s032-decision: Give a clear recommendation: for 3 services and 4 developers, a monorepo is generally the better fit
Reason: easier atomic cross-service changes, shared code/tooling/CI config, and simpler coordination for a small team
Polyrepo benefits: independent deploys/access control/ownership boundaries, which matter more with larger or separate teams
Caveat: monorepo needs CI that builds/tests only changed parts (path filters or tools like Nx/Turborepo)
Note the decision is reversible or depends on factors like language diversity, release cadence, and permissions
s033-decision: 추천: 대부분의 경우 타입스크립트를 쓰는 것이 낫다(특히 프로젝트가 커지거나 협업할 때)
이유: 정적 타입으로 버그를 일찍 잡고 자동완성/리팩터링이 좋아진다
단점: 빌드/설정 오버헤드와 학습 곡선이 있다
작은 스크립트, 프로토타입, 학습 초기에는 자바스크립트로도 충분하다
점진적 도입이 가능하다(JS 프로젝트에 TS를 단계적으로 적용)
s034-decision: 사이드 프로젝트에는 Supabase를 기본 추천하거나 명확한 기준으로 선택을 안내한다
Supabase는 Postgres 기반의 관계형 DB, SQL, 오픈소스이며 셀프호스팅 가능해 락인이 적다
Firebase는 NoSQL(Firestore), 실시간 동기화, 모바일 SDK와 구글 생태계 통합이 강점이다
둘 다 인증, 스토리지, 서버리스 함수와 넉넉한 무료 티어를 제공한다
데이터 구조(관계형 vs 문서형), 기존 숙련도, 모바일 중심 여부가 선택 기준이다
s035-decision: Give a recommendation or clear criteria rather than just listing both languages
Go: simple, quick to learn, great for backend services, cloud/DevOps tooling, concurrency with goroutines
Rust: steeper learning curve (ownership/borrow checker), but memory safety without GC, suited for systems, performance-critical, embedded, WebAssembly
Choice depends on the goal (web backend/infra vs systems programming) and current background
If unsure or wanting a faster productive start, Go first; Rust later for deeper systems understanding
s041-yesno: Yes it's syntactically allowed only inside an async callback, but it doesn't behave as expected
forEach does not wait for the async callback's promise, so iterations run concurrently and the code after the loop continues without waiting
Use a for...of loop with await for sequential execution
Use Promise.all with map for parallel execution
Error handling caveat: errors in forEach callbacks become unhandled rejections not catchable by outer try/catch
s042-yesno: No, it's not safe/recommended even for a private repo

Private repos can be exposed via collaborator access, forks, leaked access, or misconfigured visibility
Put .env in .gitignore and commit a .env.example with placeholder values instead
If already committed, rotate/revoke the keys and purge history (e.g., git filter-repo/BFG); use a secrets manager for deployment

s045-yesno: It depends: git pull will not silently overwrite uncommitted changes
If incoming changes touch files with local uncommitted modifications, git aborts the pull with an error
If the incoming changes touch different files, the pull succeeds and local changes are preserved
Untracked files can also block the pull if the incoming commits would create the same path
Safe options: commit, or git stash before pulling then git stash pop; or git pull --autostash

s072-myth: Answers no: more RAM does not always make a computer faster
RAM helps only if the current workload is running short of memory (swapping/paging)
Other bottlenecks matter: CPU, storage speed (SSD vs HDD), GPU, network
Diminishing returns beyond what workloads need; also RAM speed/channels and compatibility limits
Gives practical way to check (e.g., memory usage/pressure in Task Manager or Activity Monitor)

s081-stress: Treat the key as compromised immediately: revoke/deactivate and rotate it in the AWS IAM console first (before cleaning git)
Create a new key and update applications that used the old one
Check AWS CloudTrail / billing / Cost Explorer for unauthorized activity (EC2 instances, unexpected resources) and delete anything suspicious
Remove the secret from the repo and history (git filter-repo or BFG), noting that deleting the commit alone isn't enough since it was likely scraped
Check AWS Support notices/GuardDuty and consider contacting AWS support; enable prevention (secret scanning, pre-commit hooks, env vars/secrets manager)
Reassure that this is common and fixable if acted quickly
s082-stress: Triage quickly: confirm the issue and check what's running (e.g., active queries via pg_stat_activity / SHOW PROCESSLIST, monitoring dashboards)
Identify and kill/stop runaway or long-running queries and blocking sessions
Check recent changes (deploys, migrations, traffic spike, cron jobs) and roll back if a change is the cause
Apply mitigation: scale up/add read replicas, enable caching, rate-limit or shed load, restart connection pool
Communicate status to customers/stakeholders (status page) and escalate
After stabilization, do root-cause analysis (slow query log, missing indexes) and a postmortem
s083-stress: 진정시키기: 심호흡(예: 4초 들이쉬고 6~8초 내쉬기) 등 빠른 이완법

준비물/이동 확인(시간, 장소 또는 접속 링크, 서류), 여유 있게 도착
가벼운 움직임/물 마시기/자세 취하기, 카페인 과다와 새로운 내용 벼락치기는 피하기

Avoid risky repairs that could destroy data; prioritize file recovery over fixing the laptop
